reason: A earns more trust from commissioners who back their staff: it names the speaker, admits what he can't know (how many boats close, that bookings mask the damage at first), and offers trip logs and a catch-reporting app trial in return. B's case is similar but leans on an $80,000 three-year projection that ignores the partial recovery after 2016 and on unsupported claims (private anglers just get 'a shorter day', charters land 'the least'), and it offers the commission nothing.
